name: Triage after-hours calls from Vapi and Retell and page the on-call team

parameters.content:
## Triage after-hours calls from Vapi and Retell

A voice agent can answer the phone at two in the morning. What it cannot do is
decide whether to wake somebody. This is the backend that makes that call:
read the transcript, work out how urgent it really is, page the on-call person
only when it is warranted, and have the rest waiting in one brief at seven.

### How it works

Vapi and Retell report a finished call in different shapes, and both are read
here, along with a plain POST for testing. The transcript is the one field
both platforms document the same way, so nothing depends on a vendor summary.
A model grades that transcript against the examples of an emergency you
supply, as emergency, urgent, routine or spam, judged on what the caller said
rather than how upset they sounded. A worried person rings back three times in
five minutes, so calls from one number inside a window join a single incident
instead of paging three times, and a third call escalates on its own even when
each sounded routine. Everything is logged before anyone is paged, so a later
failure never loses the call. Ten minutes on, the incident is read again, and
the backup is paged once if nobody marked it handled. At seven, one email
lists what was escalated, who is waiting on a call back, and the rest.

### Setup

Connect Sheets, Slack, Gmail and your model. Point the Vapi server URL or
Retell webhook at this workflow, fill the Settings row, and create the Call Log
tab and the incident data table with the columns named on those nodes.

### Customization

Change the severities that escalate, the repeat window, or the ten minute wait
before the backup is paged.

## Take the call, answer the platform
Vapi, Retell and a plain POST are all read into one record. The platform is acknowledged on its own branch so it is never left waiting while triage runs.

## Grade it on what was said
A model reads the transcript against your own examples of an emergency. Repeat calls from one number join a single incident, and a third call escalates on its own.

## Log first, then wake someone
The call is written down before anyone is paged, so a later failure never loses it. The backup is paged once, ten minutes on, only if nobody marked the incident handled.

## One brief at seven
What was escalated overnight, who is waiting on a call back, then everything else. Nothing is sent after a quiet night.

options.systemMessage:
You read the transcript of a call that came in outside business hours and decide how urgent it is.

severity is exactly one of:
- emergency: someone is at risk, or something is actively causing damage or loss right now and waiting until morning makes it worse.
- urgent: needs a person today, but not in the middle of the night.
- routine: an ordinary enquiry, booking or question that the morning shift can handle.
- spam: a sales call, a wrong number, a silent call or an automated message.

Rules
- Judge from what the caller actually said, not from how loudly they said it. An angry caller asking about an invoice is routine. A calm caller reporting water coming through a ceiling is an emergency.
- If the transcript is too short or garbled to tell, use routine and say so in the summary. Never guess upward.
- summary is one sentence a person reading it at 7am can act on: what happened, to whom, and what they want.
- category is a short lowercase noun phrase, for example billing question, new booking, service fault, complaint, wrong number.
- callerName only if they gave it. Leave it empty otherwise.
- callbackNeeded is true only if the caller asked to be called back or clearly expects one.

The business will give you its own examples of what counts as an emergency. Those examples override your general judgement.

Return only the requested JSON fields.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample:
{
  "severity": "urgent",
  "category": "service fault",
  "summary": "A tenant at 14 Mill Road reports no heating since yesterday evening and has a newborn in the flat.",
  "callerName": "Priya Raman",
  "callbackNeeded": true
}
